title: Anticipation effects in DID: pre-announced policy

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Method chosen: Difference-in-Differences with an explicit anticipation (lead) term and a complementary event-study.  

Why:  
• The treatment (minimum‐capital rule) is assigned to banks below the threshold (treated = 1).  
• The rule was announced in period 3 but only enforced from period 5.  
• Standard DID (treated×post) would be biased if banks react already in periods 3-4. We therefore add an anticipation interaction (treated×announce) and, as a robustness check, estimate an event-study with period-by-treatment dummies.  

Key identifying assumptions  
1. Parallel trends: in the absence of the reform (and of any announcement) the treated and control banks would have evolved in parallel.  
2. Common anticipation window: if any behavioural change occurs before enforcement, it happens only after the public announcement (no earlier private information).  
3. No other contemporaneous shocks differentially affecting treated banks over the sample window.  

## 2. R Code
```r
# Required libraries
library(readr)      # data import
library(dplyr)      # data wrangling
library(fixest)     # high-performance FE estimators
library(ggplot2)    # event-study plot

# 1. Read the data -----------------------------------------------------------
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s10_data.csv"
df   <- read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE)

# 2. Construct timing variables ---------------------------------------------
df <- df %>% 
  mutate(announce = if_else(period >= 3 & period < 5, 1L, 0L),
         post     = if_else(period >= 5, 1L, 0L),
         treat_x_announce = treated * announce,
         treat_x_post     = treated * post)

# 3. Baseline DID with anticipation term ------------------------------------
did_mod <- feols(y ~ treat_x_announce + treat_x_post | unit_id + period,
                 data = df, cluster = "unit_id")

cat("\n== Baseline DID with anticipation term ==")
print(coeftable(did_mod), digits = 3)

# 4. Event-study (dynamic DID) ----------------------------------------------
# Relative time (0 = first post-policy period = period 5)
df <- df %>% mutate(rel_time = period - 5)

# Estimate leads/lags; reference period is rel_time = -1 (the quarter just before enforcement)
es_mod <- feols(y ~ i(rel_time, treated, ref = -1) | unit_id + period,
                data = df, cluster = "unit_id")

# Display main coefficients
cat("\n== Event study coefficients (selected) ==")
print(etable(es_mod, drop = "unit_id|period"), digits = 3)

# 5. Robustness: add unit-specific linear trends ----------------------------
df <- df %>% group_by(unit_id) %>% 
  mutate(time_trend = period - min(period)) %>% ungroup()

rob_mod <- feols(y ~ treat_x_announce + treat_x_post + 
                   treated:time_trend | unit_id + period,
                 data = df, cluster = "unit_id")

cat("\n== DID + unit-specific linear trends ==")
print(coeftable(rob_mod), digits = 3)

# 6. Optional: plot the event-study -----------------------------------------
es_plot <- broom::tidy(es_mod) %>% 
  filter(grepl("rel_time::", term)) %>% 
  mutate(rel = as.numeric(sub("rel_time::(-?\\d+).*", "\\1", term)),
         ci_low  = estimate - 1.96*std.error,
         ci_high = estimate + 1.96*std.error)

ggplot(es_plot, aes(x = rel, y = estimate)) +
  geom_point() + geom_line() +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = ci_low, ymax = ci_high), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = -1, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Event-study: treated vs control banks",
       x = "Quarters relative to enforcement (t = 0 is period 5)",
       y = "Treatment effect on Tier-1 ratio") +
  theme_minimal()
```

The script  
1. Reads the data, reconstructs `announce` and `post` flags, and interaction terms.  
2. Estimates a two-way-fixed-effects DID that separates the anticipation effect (`treated×announce`) from the enforcement effect (`treated×post`).  
3. Provides an event-study to display the full dynamic path.  
4. Adds a robustness check with bank-specific linear trends.  
5. Prints all numerics to the console; the key parameters are the coefficients on `treated×announce` (anticipation) and `treated×post` (enforcement).  

## 3. Expected Findings  
• Anticipation: a positive and significant coefficient on `treated×announce` (≈ 0.20–0.30 p.p.). Banks below the threshold start raising capital as soon as the rule is announced.  
• Enforcement: a larger positive coefficient on `treated×post` (≈ 0.40–0.60 p.p.), reflecting additional capital build-up once the rule becomes binding.  
• Event-study: insignificant leads before period 3; coefficients turn positive in periods 3-4 (anticipation window) and grow further from period 5 onward, supporting the existence of anticipation effects but also showing that the main impact materialises after the effective date.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID with anticipation — must account for pre-announcement window; use period ≤2 as clean pre-period
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Constrained banks raise capital ratios both after announcement and after effective date
